why.title: Why this exists
why.p1: Not knowing where I stood with money used to drive me mad, so more than ten years ago I started logging every expense. The first app I used was free when I began and later became a one-time purchase, which was fair enough. The habit stuck, but the app never gave me any real insight into where my money was actually going.
why.p2: For the last two years I used a budgeting app that cost quite a lot as a one-time purchase. The developer had gone quiet on known bugs, and the “native” iOS app had become painfully slow: I would wait a couple of seconds before I could type a single digit. The last straw was the Apple Watch app, which simply stopped working. The explanation was “Apple”, while everything else on the watch worked fine. It was not Apple.
why.p3: I have worked as a React Native developer for many years, shipping apps that real people use every day, and I had wanted for a long time to give something back to open source and fix this one problem: a free, local app for tracking money that is actually good and pleasant to use. I finally had the reason.
why.p4: I am happy with how it turned out. The Shortcuts automation alone removes almost all of the friction I used to have, and tags paired with categories feel so obvious that I still wonder why nobody did it. I built this with care and I intend to keep looking after it.
why.p5: Your data is yours, so if I ever get hit by a bus you can take it anywhere in a minute. I am not planning on that: I have a daughter, Olivia, on the way, and a lot to live for.

watch.title: On the wrist
watch.intro: The whole flow happens on the watch — amount, category, tags — with today's entries and your budgets a swipe away. There is a complication for the watch face, and on an Ultra you can put it on the Action button.

ipad.title: On the iPad
ipad.intro: The same app, in a column down the middle of the screen rather than a phone stretched across it — and it works in Split View. Turn on merging and your iPhone and iPad keep each other level through your own iCloud: nothing is deleted by it, and where both changed the same thing, the newer edit wins.

privacy.title: Privacy
privacy.text: Kopiyka collects nothing: there is no account and no server to send anything to. The only request it ever makes is an exchange rate from the European Central Bank.

migrate.title: Moving from another app
migrate.text: Export from your old app, hand the file and a ready-made prompt to an AI assistant, and import the result.

openSource.title: Open source
openSource.text: MIT licensed, built with React Native and a little Swift; pull requests are welcome. Android is not planned for now, but maybe later.

bug.title: Found a bug?
bug.text: Tell me and I will fix it — if the app misbehaved, Settings → Diagnostics has a crash report worth attaching.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.description: Kopiyka Budget collects nothing. Where your data lives, the one network request the app makes, and what each permission is for.

terms.title: Terms of Use
terms.description: Kopiyka Budget is free, is a personal record-keeping tool rather than financial advice, and your data is yours to keep.
